ImageDescription.value:
A must-see in Hanoi is Train Street. This metre gauge single track rail link was opened by the French in 1902 and today provides main line long distance train access to Hanoi central station from the East. These large Bo-Bo diesel electrics were built by CKD in Prague to metre gauge for Vietnam Railways. 
Trains pass just a few inches from watching crowds. Following a fatal accident late last year, the Police have tightened up on safety and security during the day - so now you have to be sitting in a trackside cafe as it passes, but at night no such restrictions exist and with the lanterns and lights of the tourist cafes swinging as they pass, night trains set out on their long journeys to far-away cities as you sip your cocktail or enjoy yet another egg-coffee.

title: File:THE ORIGINAL DUNDRUM SHOPPING CENTRE BECAME A GHOST MALL FOR A WHILE (NOW REBRANDED AS DUNDRUM VILLAGE CENTRE)-135260.jpg

ObjectName.value: THE ORIGINAL DUNDRUM SHOPPING CENTRE BECAME A GHOST MALL FOR A WHILE (NOW REBRANDED AS DUNDRUM VILLAGE CENTRE)-135260

Categories.value: Dundrum Town Centre|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2

ImageDescription.value:
It is interesting to note that some redundant elements remain from the 'Ghost Mall' days.

A few weeks ago I advised some friends from Vietnam to visit Dundrum Shopping Centre forgetting that there was an old shopping centre dating from 1971. When they told me that they were really disappointed with the place 

I was a bit surprised until I discovered that they got off the tram at the Dundrum Stop rather that the Balally stop [the next stop heading away from the city centre].

I first photographed Dundrum in December 2006 and when I visited the original shopping centre there were current Christmas Decorations and piped music but there were no traders or shoppers. All the shops displayed notices indicating that they had ceased trading or that they had relocated. My sister, who owns property including a shop, explained to me that it is possible that while all the shopkeepers may have abandoned the shopping centre they are still obliged to pay rent until the leases run out.

In 1965 the first shopping centre in Ireland was built within 100 yards of my home. Many years later the second shopping center opened in Dundrum and suddenly, Dundrum became a town, rather than a village, with a supermarket, clothes shops, a coffee shop and a record shop. We in Stillorgan were not impressed because our shopping centre was better (and in reality it was much better).

The original shopping centre in Dundrum was badly designed and there were many problems but despite this it survived until around 2005 at which time it had very few active tenants and it was not in a position to compete with the huge new centre just up the road.

A must-see in Hanoi is Train Street. This metre gauge single track rail link was opened by the French in 1902 and today provides main line long distance train access to Hanoi central station from the East. These large Bo-Bo diesel electrics were built by CKD in Prague to metre gauge for Vietnam Railways.

Travel Diary Day 12 (Travel Blog - strange-lands.com/daily/2012/07/24/sitting-on-a-car-at-br...)

3:oo am came sooner than expected. Our flight was at 6 am. I knew we’d have problems getting to the airport. We’d asked the hotel to book us a taxi. To hotel staff in Bali, tourists are little more than walking wallets and they’ll find any way to make money from you.

We made it clear to them that we wanted a metered taxi, not a private car, knowing that it would be much more expensive going privately. We told them this repeatedly. They confirmed they’d ordered a metered taxi. We knew they were lying since they get commision for referring us to private cars.

As we dragged our tired bodies to the hotel lobby the fella in reception said a private car was waiting for us. I held my temper and told him the price we were willing to pay. This was 30% less than the private car.

Some telephone calls were made and the driver decided to make his way to the hotel to sort the situation out. He hadn’t realised that I’m not a morning person. I don’t respond well to 3:00am, especially without coffee. When he walked into the office he started jabbering on. I told him to be quiet and listen. I told him the price that I was going to pay, that I was in no mood to negotiate, and that I couldn’t give a rats arse if he didn’t like it.

3 weeks of hearing the hard sell, lying, manipulation, theft (my jacket was stolen this time), had taken its toll, and I was not in the mood to negotiate. The driver just nodded and drove us to the airport.
